question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children aged 0 up to 18 months per staff member?
quote: Staff-child ratio shall be: Age Staff to Child Ratio 0 up to 18 months 1 to 5
notes: Same 1:5 applies during napping/resting (II.D.1.b.(8)). Children under 2½ must be grouped separately from older children (II.D.1.a.(2)).

question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children per staff member for children aged 2½ years up to 4 years (the age band that includes 3-year-olds)?
quote: Staff-child ratio shall be: Age Staff to Child Ratio ... 2½ years up to 4 years 1 to 11
notes: The band is 2½ up to 4 years, so it covers some 2-year-olds too. Alabama sets no fixed numeric group size.

question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children per staff member for children aged 4 years up to school age (children of lawful school age enrolled in public or private school are excluded)?
quote: Staff-child ratio shall be: Age Staff to Child Ratio ... 4 years up to school age* 1 to 18
notes: 'School age' here means children of lawful school age who are enrolled in public or private school, so a 5-year-old not yet enrolled stays at 1:18.

question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children per staff member for children aged 8 years and older?
quote: Staff-child ratio shall be: Age Staff to Child Ratio ... 8 years and older 1 to 22
notes: 8 years and older is the oldest band (1:22). Enrolled school-age children up to 8 years are 1:21.

question: Do Alabama's licensing standards for day care centers set a fixed numeric maximum group size for 4-year-olds?
quote: GROUP SIZE. The term group size is determined by the capacity of the room, age of the child, number of staff, and amount of equipment.
notes: No number is given; group size depends on room capacity (32 sq ft per child indoors), ages, staff and equipment. The ratio table repeats this definition in a footnote.

question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the minimum age for child care workers/teachers and substitutes who have primary responsibility for the care of a group of children?
quote: Child care workers/teachers and all substitutes who have primary responsibility for the care of a group of children shall be at least 18 years of age
notes: Aides/assistant teachers may be 16 but may not be counted in the staff-child ratio (II.F.1.c).

question: How many clock hours of training in administration and management must the director of a licensed day care center in Alabama have at minimum?
quote: The center director shall be at least 19 years of age and shall have at least twenty (20) clock hours of training in administration and management
notes: The director must also be at least 19, have 4 clock hours of training in quality child care, and meet one of four education/training routes (e.g. 120 clock hours of child care training plus a high school diploma/GED and 12 months' experience, or a CDA/CCP, associate or bachelor's degree with experience).

question: How many clock hours of in-service training must child care workers/teachers at a licensed day care center in Alabama obtain each year?
quote: Child care workers/teachers shall obtain at least twelve (12) clock hours of training each year.
notes: Directors need 24 hours a year and service staff 4. CPR and First Aid do not count. Staff also need at least one hour of annual training from an outside source in each of eleven areas (II.F.4.g).

question: What is the minimum indoor activity space required per child in a licensed day care center in Alabama?
quote: There shall be at least thirty-two (32) square feet of indoor activity space for each child.
notes: Bathrooms, kitchens, isolation room, office, halls used as passageways, and storage areas are not counted.

question: For a licensed day care center in Alabama first licensed, permitted or approved after January 22, 2001 with a licensed capacity of less than 60 children, what is the minimum outdoor play area per child?
quote: In centers with a licensed, permitted, or approved capacity of less than 60 children, there shall be at least 60 square feet of outdoor play area for each child.
notes: Based on licensed capacity, not on children outdoors at one time. Centers with capacity of 60 or more need 60 sq ft per child for at least half of capacity (II.C.5.b.(2)). Applies to centers licensed, permitted or approved after January 22, 2001.

question: What must a licensed day care center in Alabama have before giving a child any prescription or over-the-counter medication?
answer: An order from the child's health professional and a written, signed authorization from the parent/guardian on the required form
quote: No medication or medical procedures (prescription or over the counter) shall be administered without being ordered by the child's ... health professional and without a written, signed authorization, on the required form, from the child's parent(s)/guardian(s). Blanket authorization forms are prohibited.
notes: Both are required: a health professional's order and parent/guardian written authorization. Blanket forms are prohibited, and a form is valid for no more than seven days unless accompanied by a written physician's statement.

question: How often must emergency procedures, including fire drills, be practiced at a licensed day care center in Alabama?
quote: Drills including but not limited to fire, tornado, lock-down, and relocation. Emergency procedures shall be practiced at least once each quarter
notes: The standards set no separate fire-drill frequency; the quarterly requirement covers all emergency procedures. They recommend rotating one or more drill types each month so all drills are practiced each quarter (4 times a year).

question: How long after a child has left a licensed day care center in Alabama must the child's individual records be kept in the center?
quote: Records shall be maintained in the center for at least two (2) years after the child has left the center.
notes: Center records (attendance, transportation checklists, vehicle checks, sign-in/out sheets) are kept for the current year plus two additional years (II.H.5). Staff records: two years after the staff person leaves.

question: In a licensed day care center in Alabama, in what position must an infant younger than 12 months be placed for sleeping, unless a physician's note specifies otherwise?
quote: unless the infant has a note from a physician specifying otherwise, each infant younger than twelve (12) months, shall be placed in a supine (on his/her back) position for sleeping
notes: An infant who can easily roll from back to front is still put down on the back but may then adopt any position (II.D.2.c.(3)).

question: Within how many hours must a licensed day care center in Alabama report to the Department any injury to a child requiring professional medical treatment at the center or during away-from-center activities?
quote: The following shall be reported to the Department within 24 hours after occurrence, with written explanation to follow within five (5) days: (1) any injury requiring professional medical treatment of any child or staff person
notes: Initial report within 24 hours; written explanation within five days. The parent must be notified immediately (II.D.6.a.(2)(b)).

question: By when must a child from two months of age to lawful school age have a valid State of Alabama Certificate of Immunization (or a valid exemption) on file at a licensed day care center in Alabama?
answer: On the child's first day of attendance
quote: On the child's first day of attendance, each child from two (2) months of age to lawful school age and each child of lawful school age who is not enrolled in public or private school kindergarten shall have a valid State of Alabama Certificate of Immunization on file in the center
notes: A valid medical or religious exemption certificate, or meeting the McKinney-Vento definition of homelessness, also satisfies the rule. The certificate must be updated per its expiration date.

question: At minimum, how many staff members with current Infant-Child (Pediatric) CPR certification and a current First Aid certificate must be present during all hours of operation at a licensed day care center in Alabama?
quote: At least two (2) staff who are at least 18 years of age, who meet child care worker qualifications and have a current Infant-Child (Pediatric) Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Certification (CPR) and a current First Aid Certificate shall be present during all hours of operation.
notes: Those two must also be at least 18 and meet child care worker qualifications. II.D.6.a.(5) repeats the two-staff requirement. Pool lifeguards need their own certifications.

question: What is the minimum space required between occupied cribs in a licensed day care center in Alabama?
quote: Placement of cribs shall allow a minimum of two (2) feet of space between occupied cribs.
notes: No numeric spacing for cots; they must allow staff access and safe exit (II.D.2.d.(2)).

question: For how long is a license issued by the Alabama Department of Human Resources to a day care center valid?
quote: Licenses issued by the Department to day care centers and nighttime centers are valid for two (2) years, as shown on the license, unless revoked or suspended by the Department or voluntarily surrendered by the licensee.
notes: File the renewal application at least 30 calendar days before expiration; if filed on time and complete, the license stays in effect until the Department decides (II.B.6). A new center may first get one six-month permit.

question: During napping/resting time in a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children aged 2½ years and older per staff member?
quote: Staff-child ratio during napping/resting time shall be as follows: Ages 0 up to 18 months 18 months up to 2 ½ years 2 ½ years and older ... Staff to Child Ratio 1 to 5 1 to 14 1 to 36
notes: Nap ratios: 0 up to 18 months stays 1:5; 18 months up to 2½ years 1:14; 2½ and older 1:36. At least one qualified staff person must be in each room where children nap and able to see all of them (II.D.1.b.(7)).

question: In a multiple-age group at a licensed day care center in Alabama, the ratio for the youngest child's age category applies only if children in that youngest category make up more than what percentage of the group?
quote: When children of different ages are grouped together (multiple age grouping), staff-child ratio shall be according to the age of the youngest child in the group if more than 20% of the children are in the youngest age category.
notes: If the youngest category is 20% or less of the group, the ratio for the next highest age category applies. Children under 2½ must still be grouped separately from older children (II.D.1.a.(2)).

question: When children aged 4 years up to 6 years are in a pool two feet or more deep at a licensed day care center in Alabama, what is the maximum number of children per staff member in the pool (lifeguard not counted)?
quote: The staff-child ratio for children in the pool shall be: ... 1 staff for every 6 children ages 4 years up to 6 years;
notes: Much stricter than the regular 1:18 for this age. The ratio is set by the youngest child in the pool, counted staff must be in the pool, and the lifeguard does not count.

question: For how many days at most is a parent's medication authorization form valid at a licensed day care center in Alabama, unless accompanied by a written physician's statement?
quote: An authorization form shall be valid for no more than seven (7) days unless accompanied by a written physician's statement.
notes: Blanket authorization forms are prohibited.

question: May aides/assistant teachers (at least 16 years old) who assist with groups of children at a licensed day care center in Alabama be counted in the required staff-child ratio?
quote: Aides/assistant teachers who assist with groups of children shall be at least 16 years of age and shall: ... and shall not be counted in the required staff-child ratio.
notes: Only staff who meet child care worker qualifications (18+, high school diploma/GED) and give full attention to supervising children count (II.D.1.a.(4)).
